# Drip irrigation

## Why

Watering cans from the trough to the tunnel is 60 m each way. In the July 2023 heat I did 22 trips one evening and could not lift a teapot the next morning. Also the tomatoes want water at the roots, not on the leaves (lesson from [[Tomato blight]]).

## The kit

- Two 210 litre water butts off the shed gutter, linked at the base with a 19 mm connector
- Aquaflo gravity drip kit DK-115, £42.99 from Mole Valley Farmers: 25 m of 13 mm main pipe, 30 adjustable drippers, stakes, joiners
- Battery tap timer, Aquaflo TT-9, £24.50
- Butts raised 45 cm on breeze blocks for pressure, which is barely enough

## Settings

Drippers set to 2 litres per hour. Timer runs 6.30 am for 40 minutes, every day in July and August, every other day in June and September. Tunnel tomatoes get two drippers each; peppers one. Measured with a jam jar under one dripper for 15 minutes: 470 ml, so about 1.9 litres per hour. Close enough.

## Problems

### Leak at the elbow

The elbow joint by the tunnel door leaked from day one. Tightened it, wrapped it in PTFE tape, still dripped. In the end it was a split washer inside the timer coupling, same idea as the one in [[Leaky tap washer]], replaced with a 3/4 inch rubber one from the hardware shop in Bovey for 40p.

### Blocked drippers

Algae in the butts by August 2024. Two drippers blocked solid. Now the butts have lids and there's an inline filter, £6.

### Running dry

Two butts don't last a dry fortnight. In August 2024 I topped them up by can from the trough, which rather defeats the point. Asking the committee about a third butt on the communal shed. My running log of what gets water when is in [[Watering schedule]].
